name: Simon Mazzone
bio: is a second-year English and Creative Writing major. He is super happy to be back with the Dean’s Men, and he was previously in As Y’all Like It (Orlando), and Julius Caesar (Octavius). A painting that he thinks resonates with his portrayal of Hamlet is The Monk by the Sea, by Caspar David Friedrich. He would like to thank everyone who has worked on this show for their incredible dedication and talent, and for making him feel comfortable enough to act this emotionally unstable in front of an audience.

name: Gabbriel Bakker
bio: is a third-year Classics major on exchange from Trinity College Dublin. This is his first UT production, and he assures his mother that he is doing very well on this side of the Atlantic, despite the language barrier. Embodying the pastoral “Sower”, painted by Jean-Francois Millet, he understands Horatio as a man with big dreams and a desire to travel, confined by love and loyalty in a small court.

name: Nora Barth
bio: is a first-year Creative Writing major. This is her first show with the Dean's Men, but she has previously acted in other Shakespearian plays, including Macbeth (all Murderers), A Midsummer Night's Dream (Flute/Thisbe), and As You Like It (Rosalind). Her musical credits include SIX (Jane Seymour), Annie (Rooster), and Seussical (Horton). A painting that speaks to her role in the show is Napoleon Crossing the Alps by Jacques-Louis David, because that is unfortunately how Polonius sees himself. Ironic, isn't it, considering he dislikes the French so much.

name: Isaiah Swanson
bio: is a third-year Psychology and Fundamentals double major. This is his first show with UT. He feels very grateful to be a part of this production and thanks his friends, family, and Hamlet crew for their support. He says that a painting that speaks to his role is Caravaggio’s David with the Head of Goliath.Caravaggio made this painting at the end of his life while on the run after committing a murder. He modeled both David’s and Goliath’s face after his own to symbolize his past youth’s disappointment in his transgressions throughout his adult life.

name: Carrie Semmel
bio: is a fourth-year Political Science and Psychology major. In UT, she has previous acted in Julius Caesar (Soothsayer/Cinna the Poet/Messala), Pericles (Bolt/Knight/Fisherman/etc.), We're Live (Amanda), and Cactus Flower (Customer/Waiter). She has also played percussion in the pit for the Gilbert & Sullivan Opera Company performances of The Gondoliers. She is so incredibly happy to be working alongside all of her AMAZING castmates, who have made this entire show feel so right and perfect. She couldn't imagine a better group of people to kick off her last year at UChicago. She has chosen "Allegory of Charity" by Francesco de Mura to portray herself as a complex woman and mother. (This painting is also in the Art Institute!!)

name: Christine Hignite
bio: is a second-year English major and is so excited for the opportunity to tackle this role! This is her third UT show and she is so grateful to have gotten to know everyone in this amazing cast and crew. Previously at UChicago, she performed in Arsenic and Old Lace, Pericles, and Happy Birthday Mars Rover. She’s been acting for most of her life, but her other hobbies include writing, singing, and watching bad movies. She also performs improv with Occam’s Razor and is the current artistic director for Cup of Theatre. A painting that relates to her role in the show is Ophelia by Stanley William Hayter. (Look it up— it’s not what you’re expecting.)

name: Calister Boyd
bio: is a second-year majoring in creative writing and sociology. This is his second show with UT following a killer performance as Jonathan Brewster in Arsenic and Old Lace last spring. In the past, he's also been in The Taming of the Shrew (Petruchio) and Hadestown (Hades). He's getting really good at feeling murderous rage. The Ghost is best represented by the painting Chepstow Castle by John Martin. Laertes by Salvador Dali's Metamorphosis of Narcissus.

name: Maya Miller
bio: is a 3rd year Cognitive Science and Comparative Human Development Major. In UT, she has done The Arsonists (Assistant Stage Manager), Cactus Flower (Production Manager), Our Town (Production Manager), Antigone (Costumes), El Cepillo de Dientes (Scenic), and This is as Good as it Gets (Production Manager). A painting that reminds her of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern is Poissons de Mer by Antoine Vollon.

name: Marjane Alsterlind
bio: is a second-year and undecided about pretty much everything, including her major. This is her first performance with UT. She’s French.

name: Gavin Robalino
bio: is a fourth-year CHD major. With UT, he’s previously acted in Arsenic and Old Lace (Officer Brophy) and We’re Live (Oscar). His painting: Bold and Brash. He hopes you enjoy the show :)

name: Wren Vela
bio: is a 4th year MADD and Linguistics double major who should probably be minoring in Minecraft too tbh. He has performed in Arcadia (Gus/Augustus) and also did improv for 4 years in high school because of course he did. With the experience of a 10 year old in ballet class and a song in his heart that he should not sing, he is very excited to be here. His painting that speaks to his role is Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow by Piet Mondrian. It’s square, just like him :)
